messages.subject: Corrected BIC
parts:
Dear lavaan users,
                             we conducted a longitudinal study in which data was collected for six occasions and latent growth curve (LGC) model using lavaan was fit to the data. For some reason, we need to fit LGC for first five occasions using same longitudinal data subjects. We have a situation where we want to select model on the basis of corrected BIC (CBIC). We know that model with lower CBIC should be preferred.  My question is, whether these two LGC models (Six occasions vs five occasions) be compared and selection of model with lower CBIC can be made?

 any suggestions or pointer to relevant literature will be highly appreciated.  
 Thank you in advance !

compute it manually. The ingredients should be in

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Corrected BIC
parts: My question is, whether these two LGC models (Six occasions vs five occasions) be compared and selection of model with lower CBIC can be made?

For the 2 CBICs to be comparable, they need to be fit to the same data.  I have no idea why a 5-occasion vs 6-occasion LGC would be competing models -- the 6-occasion model is potentially just an extrapolation of the 5-occasion model to include a 6th occasion using the same growth parameters.  If you want to compare the CBICs from these two models you would have to include the data from the 6th occasion in the 5-occasion model.  You could simply saturate the 6th occasion measurements by allowing them to freely correlate with the residuals of the measurements on the first 5 occasions -- as if the 6th occasion measurements were auxiliary variables in a FIML estimation of the 5-occasion model.  Then both models would be fit to the same data, but the 6th occasion measurements would not add any degrees of freedom to the 5-occasion model, nor should they unduly influence the growth parameters fit to the 5 occasions.

Terry
